Measured directly against DataSF's real curb and centerline data: the blocks' south edge (the recorded Assessor lot line) sits ~9.5-10.3m from the street centerline, real curb ~7.2-7.8m -- a genuine ~2.7-3.5m sidewalk gap the blocks already stop short of. column5: Mission Rock labeled map, round 2: the round-1 street-corridor fix above unioned in a real DataSF curb LineString that turns out to cover only part of Block H's Mission Rock St frontage, pulling the rendered street edge in tight under part of H (~1.2m gap) while the rest of the D1/D2/H frontage kept the generic ~3.9-4.3m gap -- a false pinch/step the owner flagged as looking wrong ('should be a straight line'). Checked the block geometry first rather than assume it was wrong: D1, D2 and H's south edges are collinear to within millimeters from their own committed coordinates, and the pure centerline buffer (no curb) already runs as one continuous straight band the full frontage length at the same bearing. Added an include_curbs flag to street_geometry.build_street_buffer() (default True, unchanged for every clipping/QA caller) and set it False only for this one map's rendering, so a partial curb segment can't make an already-straight real street look broken on the one map built to show it plainly. No geometry or clipping logic changed.
